title: Historical snapshot identity vs current contract identity

scope.idea: Historical provenance and current interface compatibility must remain independently verifiable facts.

past.summary: Lotus fixture events were produced against a historical LiminalDB snapshot and exact AuditEvent contract blob.

present.summary: LiminalDB main advanced, while the consumed protocol-types.ts bytes remained exactly unchanged.

future.summary: Compatibility is evaluated from exact current contract bytes while historical adapter commit remains provenance rather than a permanent semantic key.

evidence.claim: Historical AuditEvent contract blob is fd733971aaae089df770062bcf7f2c2d6d19ca1d.
Current main exposes the same exact contract blob.
v0.1 required adapter.commit to equal one historical LiminalDB commit in addition to the contract blob.
v0.2 computes the Git blob SHA of the current checked-out contract and compares event-declared contract identity against those exact bytes.
Tests prove unchanged historical artifacts remain compatible when bytes match and fail when the declared contract blob diverges.

causalPath.statement: The v0.1 verifier used one historical repository commit as both provenance identity and semantic compatibility identity.
LiminalDB main advanced while the consumed AuditEvent contract bytes remained unchanged.
A semantically compatible historical artifact could be rejected solely because the repository snapshot identity changed.
Keep historical adapter.commit as provenance, but determine current compatibility by hashing the actual checked-out contract bytes and requiring exact declared blob equality.

navigation.reason: The apparent stale-base problem resolves only after separating repository-snapshot time from interface-content identity.

refactor.change: Replace permanent historical-commit equality with current checked-out contract-blob verification while preserving full historical adapter SHA as provenance.
refactor.expectedEffect: Repository evolution no longer creates false incompatibility when the interface is byte-identical, while actual contract drift still fails closed.
